commons.title: Casa Museo de Luis Alberto Acuña 64.JPG
commons.description:
Le peintre et le sculpteur L.A. Acuña (1904-1994) fut nettement influencé par les travaux de Picasso et l'art précolombien.
Installé dans une belle demeure, qui mérite une visite à elle seule, ce musée présente de nombreuses oeuvres de l'artiste colombien, ainsi que des pièces archéoloiguqes mises au jour par  l'artiste et ses amis. Le patio, dans lequel on peut admirer une peinture murale et des sculptures de l'artiste, témoigne de la fascination de ce dernier pour la mythologie et les contes indigènes.

Featuring works by one of Colombia's most influential painters, sculptors, writers and historians, who was inspired by sources ranging from Muisca mythology to contemporary art. This museum has been set up in the mansion where Acuña (1904–93) lived for the last 15 years of his life and is Colombia's most comprehensive collection of his work.
commons.editorial_reason: Image shows a modern artist's museum and works inspired by indigenous mythology, not clearly Muisca cultural material.

commons.title: Gold Museum, Bogota (36145671394).jpg
commons.credit: Pedro Szekely from Los Angeles, USA
commons.description: Muisca raft in the Gold Museum, Bogotá, Colombia. This raft made of gold was found in Pasca, Cundinamarca, in 1969, and is associated with the legend of El Dorado, representing the ceremony that used to take place in Lake Guatavita where the zipa would cover his body in gold dust and drop gold and emerald offerings into the lake.
commons.editorial_reason: Gold Muisca raft from Pasca, explicitly tied to the El Dorado ceremony; visible Muisca cultural artifact.
